title: The Sunken Bell of Mistmoor
pitch: In the fog-bound fen-village of Mistmoor, the great bronze warning bell has fallen silent — and a fisher has vanished. The villagers whisper of the drowned dead, but something with greener hands toppled that bell. One evening's work to set it right.

scenes.title: Mistmoor Green
scenes.summary: Dusk over a huddle of stilt-houses ringing a muddy green. Across the fen, the old bell-tower stands dark and crooked. Edda Marsh, the elderly bellkeeper, meets the party — grateful but evasive (she quietly paid the raiders to move on, and is ashamed). Truths to uncover: the bell fell three nights ago; the fisher Tomen has been missing since; lights have been seen in the tower; small, clawed footprints lead toward it. Suggested checks (offer multiple paths, never gate the only route): Wisdom (Insight) DC 12 to sense Edda is hiding something; Charisma (Persuasion) DC 13 to coax the truth; Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) DC 12 to find the goblin tracks. Any one success points the party at the tower.

scenes.title: The Drowned Bell-Tower
scenes.summary: A half-sunken stone tower at the fen's edge. The great bell lies cracked in the mud, its heavy iron clapper torn free and gone. Cookfire smoke and gnawed bones betray a camp below. Three ways in — deliberately redundant so a party missing any one skill is fine: a slick climb to a broken upper window (Strength (Athletics) DC 12); a silent wade through the reeds to the undercroft stair (Dexterity (Stealth) DC 12); or simply walking in the gap in the wall (no check — but the goblins hear them coming and act first). A Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Survival) DC 12 spots a string-and-tin alarm rigged across the stair.

scenes.title: The Undercroft
scenes.summary: Ankle-deep black water and a guttering fire. Two goblins bicker over the stolen iron clapper (they mean to sell it to a marsh-witch downriver) while their rat gnaws in a corner. The missing fisher, Tomen, is here — bound, gagged, and alive. This is the set-piece combat, unless the party engineered a cleverer resolution (a convincing bluff, a bargain, picking them off by stealth). The goblins use Nimble Escape to dart and hide; once reduced to a single combatant, the survivor tries to flee with the clapper. Freeing Tomen and recovering the clapper resolves the adventure; rehanging the bell is the quiet denouement.
